mkdir -p /tmp/scr_esc && cat > /tmp/scr_esc/esc.py <<'EOF'
import re, glob, os, collections
base = "/tmp/r2run-wf_0krt4/data/text"
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(base, "*.txt")))
print("files", len(files))
rows = []
for f in files:
    txt = open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    pages = re.split(r"=== page \d+", txt)
    for p in pages:
        m = re.search(r"Case Number:\s*(\S+)", p)
        if not m: continue
        r = re.search(r"recommends the following civil penalty:(.*?)Abstentions", p, re.S | re.I)
        rec = r.group(1) if r else ""
        if re.search(r"ticket\s+escalation", rec, re.I):
            # headline penalty
            s = rec.replace("$$", "$")
            pm = re.search(r"\$\s?([\d,]+(?:\s?\d{3})*)", s)
            pen = None
            if pm:
                pen = int(re.sub(r"[,\s]", "", pm.group(1)))
            rows.append((os.path.basename(f), m.group(1), pen, rec.strip().replace("\n"," | ")[:120]))
print("cases with ticket escalation:", len(rows))
c = collections.Counter(r[2] for r in rows)
print(c.most_common())
for r in rows[:5]: print(r)
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/scr_esc/esc.py

**Tool limitation:** Bash is disabled in this session, so I could not run a per-case parser. I had to work from Grep line matches and a few direct reads.

**Escalation count (estimate): roughly 200 to 250 cases.**
- A plain search for "ticket escalation" (any capitalization) returns about 204 lines across the 58 order texts, after excluding the unchecked checkbox template lines in ord_PSD_042121.
- The search misses phrases split across a line break (for example, "no ticket" / "escalation" in ord_PSD_083022 and ord_PSD_110823). A second search found many more of these, so the true total is higher than 204.
- Some cases contain the phrase twice (once in the penalty line and again in "Additional Information"), which overstates the case count. Without a per-case parse I cannot remove those duplicates exactly.
